content.title: About
content.content: Beef NFS (non‑fabricated sort) is a whole cut of meat from cattle that has not undergone additional processing. It offers a rich flavor, firm texture and is suitable for grilling, roasting, braising and pan‑searing.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
It contains more iron than most other meats, making it a valuable source of this mineral.
NFS cuts are often chosen by restaurants for steaks because they retain the natural taste and juiciness.
The color of beef can vary with myoglobin levels; darker meat indicates higher myoglobin content.
Beef is rich in creatine, which supports muscle energy metabolism.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is crucial for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Creatine and carnitine
items.content: These compounds help improve endurance and energy metabolism.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake can contribute to elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor pathogens such as E. coli or Salmonella.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beef can be grilled, roasted, braised, boiled or used in stews. For steaks, let the meat reach room temperature before cooking and aim for the desired doneness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store beef in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for up to 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator rather than at room temperature.
